::: note
[About this page]{.tag}
This page lets you look at what team claude **measured** in experiment E4 of the race pilot: conditional generative models of the saturated ABC-forced dynamo in 3D incompressible MHD (grid 16³, 665 Fourier modes, ν = 0.05, η from 0.03 to 0.08), with constraints imposed through the model design, the training loss or the sampling procedure. Every number comes from a result file written by a committed script and exported by `experiments/export_explorer.py --team claude`; nothing here is published or reviewed outside this repository. The text, the proofs and the status of each claim are in the [internship report](../report/index.html) ([PDF](../report/index.pdf)).
:::

## Controls {#controls}

</div>

## Data and models {#downloads}

The reference data of E4, the laws that the report cites and a catalogue of both are published as the release [e4-data-v1.0](https://github.com/knoel99/milady-2027/releases/tag/e4-data-v1.0) of the repository; the section [Data and models](../report/index.html#sec-release) of the report says what they are. The data are a draw generated for the release by the committed script, and the models are the cited laws retrained on these data on CPU: the weights of the GPU runs behind the report were not kept.

<!-- e4:releasepage:begin -->
- The release is not built yet.
<!-- e4:releasepage:end -->

Reload a law and draw samples, from a checkout of the repository (the script downloads the files it needs and checks their SHA-256):

```bash
python3 experiments/e4_release_example.py --dir e4_release --download --law W16 --seed 0 --eta 0.04899 --n 256 --out samples.h5
```

```python
import sys; sys.path[:0] = ["src", "experiments"]
import e4_release_example as R
for name in (R.SPACE, R.WEIGHTS.format(seed=0)):
    R.fetch("e4_release", name)                # download, check the SHA-256
space = R.load_space("e4_release")             # latent space and its normalisation
w9 = R.load_w9("e4_release", space, seed=0)    # flow-matching model W9
fields = R.to_fields(space, R.sample_w9(w9, space, eta=0.04899, n=64))   # u and B: (64, 16, 16, 16, 3)
```

A data file is read with `milady.data.read_mff(path)` and checked with `python -m milady.data.convert validate --full <file>`.
